source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第二节

scope: Explicit chest/limb-lead T-contour teaching templates, not etiological or ischemic presets.

notes: Landmark positions and equal-amplitude biphasic shapes are authored choices. T onset/end and QT are preserved; interpolation runs directly between positive and negative peaks without a flat zero-crossing knot.

crossingTiming: Biphasic T permits a zero-crossing position of 1-999 permille; null or 500 preserves original timing. Extrema lie at the crossing plus/minus half the shorter adjacent span. Phase speed changes only at extrema, without an extra slope discontinuity at zero. Not applicable to notched T; not an etiological parameter.
limitations: No cause is inferred for notched or biphasic T waves.
ST-T fusion and other ventricular editing modes must be disabled.
Windows behavior is not yet manually verified.
Only one limb-lead target at a time; all six limb leads cannot be set independently.
limbProjection: I/II/III target differences are injected through paired positive/negative electrode bands. Augmented leads use 2/-1/-1, with 2 formed by duplicating the same band rather than rescaling. Each band's electrode increments sum to zero, preserving Wilson and chest leads while other limb leads follow projection identities. Integer division of target differences may leave Q32 rounding residue.
symmetricInverted: Symmetric inverted T teaching contour: -1000*[4*x*(1-x)]^3, peaking halfway through T with zero endpoint potentials/slopes. Normalized curvature is authored; amplitude is explicit. QT is not automatically prolonged and no cause is inferred.
peakedUpright: Peaked T teaching contour: 1000*[4*x*(1-x)]^8, with a positive midpoint peak, symmetric sides and zero endpoint potentials/slopes. Exponent 8 and full-T support are authored to produce a narrower peak. QT is not automatically shortened; this is not a hyperkalemia/ischemia preset. Peak amplitude is explicit.
broadUpright: Broad tall T teaching contour: normalized x^5*(1-x)^3, peaking at 62.5%, wider than the peaked template, with a longer rise and shorter fall. Endpoint potentials/slopes are zero. Polynomial and peak position are authored; amplitude is independent. T/QT are preserved without automatic ST elevation or etiological inference.
monophasic: Reuses asymmetric reference-T landmarks and smooth interpolation normalized to unit peak. Upright/ordinary inverted monophasic shapes allow explicit 0-4000 uV peak amplitude; zero flattens the target T. Low amplitude is a demonstration, not a separate diagnostic threshold. T/QT are preserved; polarity follows shape selection.
independentBiphasicPeaks: The second-lobe peak may be null or 1-4000 uV for biphasic T only. Null/equal peaks preserve previous bytes. Unequal peaks map normalized absolute potential u by g(u)=m*u+(a-m)*u^2, where m is the smaller peak and a is the respective lobe amplitude. Both zero-point derivatives equal m; the map is monotone and bounded, preserving zero/extremum phases. This is an authored morphology transform; sampled derivatives still depend on LUT linear interpolation.
